subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'm planning a crouched gargoyle pose on a stone ledge, facing forward with low haunches, forearms planted on the ledge edge, wings folded behind, tail curled down the side, and head raised with horns forward.

For construction I'll stick to the builder's core API—joints, chains, sweeps—and keep the stone material as a mottled, countershaded paint with moss accents, plus a glow kit for orange eyes. Now I'm working out the skeleton, defining the ledge height and placing the hip origin, then sketching the spine as a catmull curve rising from the hips toward the chest and neck base.

Now I'm laying out the neck chain extending from the spine's end up to the head joint, assigning parent relationships between hips, spine, and neck, then building the body as a sweep along the spine path with radius values that widen through the chest.

Working out the head's local coordinate frame so I can place skull geometry relative to its forward/up/right directions, using a box shape positioned slightly forward and up from the head bone origin.

Switching to a simpler approach: defining all head parts with explicit model-space offsets from a fixed head-joint point (HP), with +z as forward, rather than relying on bone-local axes. Starting to lay out the skull box and brow ridge dimensions and positions using this scheme.

Continuing with the jaw structure — a snout box with small nostril spheres, a lower jaw attached to a jaw bone with its own joint and chin placement, and teeth built from cone-shaped fangs using a spike helper function for both upper and lower sets.

For the head details, I'm sweeping bezier curves from the skull base backward to form curving horns with tapering radius, adding pointed ear spikes jutting outward, and building eye sockets as dark glowing spheres with a separate textured plane carrying an SVG slit-pupil eye design with orange glow and ink outlines.

I'm positioning the eye planes carefully relative to the snout box and brow geometry so they sit just beneath the brow ridge at the correct depth, and planning additional chin beard spikes and brow spikes for extra detail.

Now I'm moving to the legs, working out a crouched stance with large haunch spheres at the hips connecting through multi-segment limbs with bends down to the feet.

I'm sketching manual joint coordinates for the leg chain rather than relying on IK, placing hip, knee, ankle, and toe points to form a lion-like crouched posture, then considering how to connect them as a polyline with sharp joints.

Naming the chain ["hipL","kneeL","ankleL","toeL"] so the extra name creates a tip segment (footL), parented under the hips joint with role "leg", and tapering the sweep radii down the limb. I'm also planning a flattened thigh sphere at the haunch and small forward-facing claw cones at the toes.

Working out the toe spikes and foot block geometry, referencing the chain's last joint as the tip, then sketching shoulder-to-elbow placements for the crouched front arms planted forward.

Continuing down each arm to the wrist and clawed hand tip, naming the joint chain shoulderL/elbowL/wristL/handL, parenting to the chest spine joint, tapering radii, and adding curved claw spikes plus a shoulder ball joint before moving on to the folded wings.

For the wings I'm plotting the bone chain from shoulder root through elbow and wrist out to the tip, keeping them tucked slightly open behind the back, then building three fanned finger chains from the wrist with membrane surfaces stretched between adjacent fingers and down to the body attachment point, making sure each membrane edge pair runs consistently from root to tip for proper resampling.

I'll keep fingers as simple chains with a single span and name, and use chains for the membrane edges too, with the third edge running from wrist to body point using the wrist bone. For the wing arm, I'll parent it to the chest joint and name the chain segments for upper arm, elbow, and wrist.

Now I'm working out the actual spatial coordinates for the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints relative to the crouched body height, aiming for an extended, readable wing pose as described in the brief, then placing finger joints branching outward from the wrist.

I'll close that triangular trailing edge between the wingtip and body point, keeping it simple. For the membrane, I'm setting the thickness to about 1.2% of the wing width, and planning the coloring so the wings are darker stone with a ribbed, batlike texture on the skin.

Now I'm working out the tail and ledge geometry: positioning the ledge as a wide, shallow box extending along the depth axis, then tracing the tail's path from the hips backward so it curls down over the ledge's rear edge, adjusting the curl to sweep toward one side rather than straight back.

For the tail itself, I'm laying out a looping path of points on the ledge top with decreasing radius from base to tip, aiming for a spade-shaped end, and I'm sketching how many joints the sweep needs and tuning the tail's minimum height so the spade tip touches the ledge surface correctly while orienting the diamond-shaped tip along the tail's end tangent.

For the dorsal spikes, I'm planning to place them along the body's spine sweep using evenly spaced points, giving each a small radius and length with bone-driven placement, and I'm checking how the sweep's surface-point function should be called to position them correctly.

I'm skipping chest ribs, but considering adding a decorative quatrefoil medallion decal to the chest, figuring out how to locate the chest-front point on the body sweep using azimuth/elevation surface queries.

Then I'm thinking through the ledge geometry: a stone-textured block with a cornice slab on top, sizing the main block versus the slightly larger top slab and stacking their heights.

Now I'm adding a dentil row of small repeated boxes along the front edge, and layering a carved gothic arcade texture plane onto the ledge's front face, using dark lines on a transparent background so the arches read as cut-outs rather than solid fills.

For the stone material, I'm defining a procedural paint shader that blends base tones with noise, darkens recessed cracks, brightens upward-facing lit surfaces, and adds patchy moss coloring where the surface faces upward and a secondary noise pattern exceeds a threshold.

Now I'm planning the creature's structure: adding soot-darkened variants, glowing eye textures, rib and shoulder-blade detailing on the torso, and helper functions for claws and fangs. I'm also working out how to pose the jaw bone open slightly after building its parts, keeping the whole part count around 150 while staying reasonably compact.

I'm figuring out the joint hierarchy — placing the mouth interior with a tongue, defining the jaw joint's position and forward aim parented to the head, then chaining the neck joints from the spine's end point up to the head joint, with the head and arms both parenting off the final spine joint near the chest.

Now I'm checking body proportions against the spine path points: verifying the chest radius keeps the belly just clear of the ledge, the hip and haunch spheres sit at reasonable heights above the ground, and the neck sweep connects smoothly into the head and skull radius.

With geometry settled, I'm moving to writing the actual rendering code, setting up color constants for the dark body and glow accents, and building a small helper function for placing parts relative to bones and coordinates.

Still working out the eye glow and brow geometry, then placing upper and lower fang spikes with their own base positions and lengths...

Now sizing the jaw box so it closes properly against the snout, adding small cone teeth rows, tweaking the jaw pose angle, and placing a tongue and dark interior box. I'm also adding a chin goatee spike, ear spikes with their own direction and bone thickness, and setting up a claw helper function to attach claws to the crouched gargoyle's hands and fingers.

Positioning the arm geometry now — hand tips, wrists, elbows, and shoulders with their coordinates, plus a tapered tube for the arm connecting these points with rounded caps.

I'm setting up the foot points next: toe, ankle, and the shin running from knee to ankle to toe. Then I'm defining the rig joint naming scheme using side labels (L/R) and building the leg chain as a four-point polyline from hip through knee, ankle, to toe, with the arm chain following a similar pattern.

Still defining the wing and finger chains...

Setting the wing membrane color to the darker stone shade for rib definition, and sizing the arm sweep radii down toward the wingtip. I'm adding a thumb claw spike angled up-forward at the wrist, then moving to the tail: five chain points parented to the hips, tapering radius from 0.1 to 0.03, with small spines and a spade tip.

Now I'm wiring up the hips as the root joint, parenting both the tail and spine chains to it, and leaving the orientation default. I'm skipping the rain-spout gargoyle detail but adding a subtle water-stain paint mark, and attaching the ledge prop directly to the hips bone. I'm also placing small claw spikes along the wing finger directions, adding a spiky mane collar around the back of the neck, and positioning a chest decal near the front torso surface.

Writing SVG code...

Checking that the module-level paint definitions still work fine before the builder, then I'll pull everything together into the final code.
